# definitions
p_value: is the smallest significance level at which the data lead to rejection of the null
hypothesis. It gives the probability that data as unsupportive of H0 as those observed will occur when H0 is true. 
a small p value is a strong indication that the null hypothesis is not true. The smaller tha p value, the greater the evidence for the falsity of H0. 
It is related to the test_statistic.


# hypothesis testing steps
  
1 Write the hypothesis and alpha level 
2 Choose statistics
3 Rejection rule
4 Calculation
5 Conclusion

1 a claim from manufacturer is normally in the H0

# Distributions
Bernoulli: E[X] = p, Var(X) = p(1-p)
Binomial: E[X]=  np,   Var(X) = np(1-p)
Chi_squared:          Var(X) = its degrees of freedom = n.

# Type II error

The probability of making a type II error is controlled by the sample size.( more sample datapoints, lower probability)

Concept                Symbol   Meaning: 
Type I Error           alpha    reject h0 when h0 is true
Type II Error           beta    fail to reject when h0 is false
Power of a Test      1- beta    the probabilty of correctly rejecting h0 when it is false.

type II error -> you miss the real effect
power of a test -> you detect a real effect.

# Multiple Comparisons Procedures
c = k(k-1) /2 # k is the number of group
expected number of rejecting H0 when it is true: a*c
a*c/c = a -> the rate of type I error

## bonferroni
individual test alpha = a/c
family wise test alpha = 1-(1-a)*c
